# Responses by Region Plot
```{r}
#install.packages("maps")
library(maps)

bag <- read.csv("WhatsinYourBag_Public.csv")

# count responses by state abbreviation
state_counts <- table(bag$Region)
state_counts <- state_counts[names(state_counts) %in% state.abb]

# convert abbreviations to full lowercase state names
state_names <- tolower(state.name[match(names(state_counts), state.abb)])

# draw base map
map("state", fill = TRUE, col = "white", bg = "lightblue", mar = c(0,0,2,0))
title("Responses by State")

# shade states pink: darker pink = more responses
for(i in seq_along(state_names)) {
  intensity <- as.numeric(state_counts[i]) / max(state_counts)
  shade <- rgb(1, 0.8 - 0.5*intensity, 0.9 - 0.6*intensity)
  
  map("state",
      regions = state_names[i],
      fill = TRUE,
      add = TRUE,
      col = shade,
      border = "black")
}
state_counts
```


# Most Unique Items People Carry
```{r}
bag <- read.csv("WhatsinYourBag_Public.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


# Category labels were derived from the original open-ended responses before public release.
# Only anonymized categories are shared to protect survey respondents.
bag$UniqueItem_clean <- bag$UniqueItemCategory

final_counts <- as.data.frame(sort(table(bag$UniqueItem_clean), decreasing = TRUE))
names(final_counts) <- c("Category", "Count")

#
par(mar = c(5, 12, 4, 4))  # a little more room

x_max <- max(final_counts$Count) * 1.25  # add space on the right

bp <- barplot(final_counts$Count,
              names.arg = final_counts$Category,
              horiz = TRUE,
              las = 1,
              col = "lightblue",
              border = NA,
              main = "Unique Items by Category",
              xlab = "Count",
              cex.names = 0.9,
              cex.main = 1.3,
              cex.lab = 1.1,
              xlim = c(0, x_max))

text(x = final_counts$Count + max(final_counts$Count)*0.03,
     y = bp,
     labels = final_counts$Count,
     cex = 0.8,
     pos = 4)

```
